title: Principality of Abkhazia
capsule: The Principality of Abkhazia was a feudal lordship of the Sharvashidze (Chachba) dynasty along the northeastern Black Sea coast of the South Caucasus, emerging as a distinct entity in the second half of the 15th century amid the fragmentation of the unified Kingdom of Georgia. Nominally subordinate to the neighbouring princes of Mingrelia, the Sharvashidze in practice exercised broad autonomy and, from the 16th century onward, accepted Ottoman suzerainty, with the coastal fortress of Sukhum-Kale (Sukhumi) garrisoned by the Ottomans. Caught between Ottoman and an expanding Russian presence, Prince Kelesh Ahmed-Bey and his successors shifted patronage toward St. Petersburg, and in 1810 the principality formally entered the Russian Empire as an autonomous protectorate while retaining its native dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the principality's boundaries fluctuated with overlapping Ottoman and Megrelian claims, and no detailed cartographic record survives for most of its history.
